cards.label: Model answer 1 of 3
cards.title: Polar form
cards.body: Write \(z = |z|e^{i\,\mathrm{Arg}\,z}\) with \(-\pi < \mathrm{Arg}\,z \le \pi\). The principal \(n\)th root is \(z^{1/n} = |z|^{1/n} e^{i\,\mathrm{Arg}\,z/n}\), or equivalently \(|z|^{1/n}\left(\cos\frac{\mathrm{Arg}\,z}{n} + i\sin\frac{\mathrm{Arg}\,z}{n}\right)\).

cards.title: Natural domain
cards.body: The natural domain is the whole complex plane: every \(z\) has a principal \(n\)th root, and \(z = 0\) is mapped to \(0\). The root is single valued because the argument is restricted before dividing by \(n\).

cards.title: Visualising F
cards.body: Going once around the origin on the surface moves from one sheet to the other, and going twice returns to the start. So \(F(z) = z^{1/2}\) is single valued on the surface, which makes its two branches easy to see.

cards.label: Key points
cards.title: Remember
points: z^2 is one-to-one on D and maps D onto C minus {0}
Inverse of z^2 on D: sqrt(|z|) e^{i Arg(z)/2}, the principal root
Rays arg z = +-pi/2 both map to arg w = pi; only pi/2 lies in D
Principal root: branch cut on the negative real axis
Riemann surface: two sheets cut along the negative real axis, glued crosswise
